narrative.title: Depth Gauge for the Kernel Trace Line
narrative.scenario: A kernel debug logger writes each trace as a single balanced line where every nested subroutine call adds one more layer of parentheses around its own sub-expression. The profiler's summary reports how deep the call stack ever gets — the largest number of parentheses that are simultaneously open at any point of the line. Digits and operators are noise; only the brackets move the gauge.
narrative.inputFormat: A valid parentheses string s containing digits, the operators '+', '-', '*', '/', and the parentheses '(' and ')'.
narrative.outputFormat: The nesting depth of s — the maximum count of simultaneously open parentheses at any point in the string.
constraints: s is a valid parentheses string: every '(' has a matching ')' in order

testCases.explanation: The term (8)/4 sits inside three simultaneously open pairs — the deepest point of the line.
The three bracket groups nest one, two, and three levels deep, so the deepest group sets the answer.

hintLevels: Level 1: Depth only changes at brackets — digits and operators never move the gauge.
Level 2: Sweep once with a counter: increment on '(', decrement on ')', and remember the highest value the counter ever reaches.
Level 3: Raise the running maximum immediately after each opening bracket, because the peak can only occur right after a '(' — a full stack is never needed, just one integer.
